attributes.probed_form: All three probes edit BOTH twin sites identically (src/game/game/player.c lines 2124-2130 and 2155-2161 at HEAD 0f45ae610). BASELINE FORM at both sites: `for (j = 0; j < 4; j++) {` / `    s32 st;` / blank / `    if (j != i && (st = PT(j)->state) != 0 && st != 2 && st != 3) {` / `        break;` / `    }` / `}`. PROBE A (REVERTED), unconditional block-top initialiser: `for (j = 0; j < 4; j++) {` / `    u8* jrec = (u8*)potionicon_tab + j * PREC_STRIDE;` / `    s32 st;` / blank / `    if (j != i && (st = PF(jrec, 0xC40 + 0xE8, s32)) != 0 && st != 2 && st != 3) {` / `        break;` / `    }` / `}`. PROBE B (REVERTED), declaration AND assignment both inside the short-circuit: `for (j = 0; j < 4; j++) {` / `    if (j != i) {` / `        u8* jrec = (u8*)potionicon_tab + j * PREC_STRIDE;` / `        s32 st;` / blank / `        if ((st = PF(jrec, 0xC40 + 0xE8, s32)) != 0 && st != 2 && st != 3) {` / `            break;` / `        }` / `    }` / `}`. PROBE C (REVERTED) is probe B with the two declarations moved out to the loop-body block top and the initialiser split into a plain assignment -- i.e. B's `if (j != i) {` line is preceded by `    u8* jrec;` and `    s32 st;`, and B's `        u8* jrec = (u8*)potionicon_tab + j * PREC_STRIDE;` / `        s32 st;` pair inside the if becomes the single line `        jrec = (u8*)potionicon_tab + j * PREC_STRIDE;`. Nothing else differs; this is the form claim.law.PC_a-named-pointer-local-selects-the-displacement-load-and-its-declaration-site-decides-the-hoist predicts should behave like A. The `PF(jrec, 0xC40 + 0xE8, s32)` spelling is not invented here: it is the idiom already standing at lines 1729-1731 and 1853-1855 in this same function, neither of which appears in any residual cluster.

hypothesis.statement: THE COUPLING PREMISE THIS RECORD ORIGINALLY BANKED IS REFUTED BY ITS OWN PROBE-A OUTPUT, AND THE REAL LEAD IS THAT PROBE A'S RESIDUAL AT THE TWO TWINS IS PERMUTATION-CLASS. Refutation first, so no lane spends a probe on it: probe A closed both j-loop twins while leaving the two ours-only `mr` at +0x5d8/+0x670 textually UNCHANGED -- they are still in probe A's multiset as `-2 mr`, and its cluster rows at +0x5d8/+0x5e4/+0x678 are identical to baseline's. The two components therefore move INDEPENDENTLY, the `r19` base cache is not a shared cause, and the earlier co-occurrence across probes G/I/J was correlation from forms that happened to disturb both. Consequently the 12t basin is NOT a floor imposed by one mechanism. The untried work: after probe A the twins are no longer an addressing-form difference at all but a PURE ONE-SLOT REORDER of two relocation-free atoms -- ours issues `add`+`lwz` before the `beq` that short-circuits `j != i`, the target issues them after, with the same opcodes, the same registers and no other word changed in either window. That is the shipped instruction_permutation class, over a 2-atom window at each twin, and this record now supplies the source-exhaustion provenance the Mandatory result policy requires (three literal axes, with the B/C pair proving the ordering is not selectable from source). The open question is arbitration, and it must be settled BEFORE any rule is authored: probe A's fresh fuzzy is 96.8433 against baseline's 97.2692, so a rule built on it starts from a state the project scores WORSE, and whether closing both twins recovers more than 0.4259 is unmeasured. Measure the post-permutation fuzzy first; if it does not clear 97.2692, the honest outcome is that this function's two candidate states are both local optima and neither is a keep.
